harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory with the sticky bit (mode 1777, owned root:root), so any user can create files but only the file owner (or root) can remove/rename them. Verified with two test users: cross-user delete is rejected (Operation not permitted) while own-file delete succeeds and other-user creation succeeds. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 via sudo reboot, polled through the outage until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified /srv/drop's permissions, sticky-bit deny-delete behavior, and pre-existing file data all survived the restart.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop, set owner root:root and mode 1777 (world-writable + sticky bit)
Created testuser1 and testuser2 to validate multi-user behavior
Verified testuser1 can create a file and testuser2 cannot delete it (sticky bit enforced)
Verified testuser2 can create its own file and testuser1 can delete its own file
Captured pre-restart boot_id and /srv/drop state as baseline
Issued a native reboot on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions, sticky-bit delete-denial behavior, and persisted file data after restart

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop exists as shared writable directory with sticky bit (mode 1777, root:root)
evidence.summary: stat shows '1777 root:root /srv/drop' and ls -ld shows drwxrwxrwt after mkdir/chown/chmod

evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (sticky bit enforcement)
evidence.summary: testuser1 created file_from_user1.txt; testuser2's rm attempt failed with 'Operation not permitted'; file still present afterward

evidence.requirement: Directory remains usable: any user can create files, owners can delete their own files
evidence.summary: testuser2 created file_from_user2.txt successfully; testuser1 deleted its own file_from_user1.txt successfully

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6 and /srv/drop state (1777 perms, file_from_user2.txt present) before restart
sudo reboot issued via backgrounded nohup; command returned 'reboot acknowledged' with exit_code 0 before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node polled until exec available again after restart
evidence.summary: Two connection-timeout failures, then connection-reset, then successful exec confirms outage and recovery of node1's exec path

evidence.requirement: Proof that boot identity changed (actual restart, not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6 to b356d23e-2f8b-4164-922b-c2075ef80dee, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required configuration, data, and behavior
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/drop still 1777 root:root, prior file_from_user2.txt persisted, and sticky-bit delete-denial re-verified end-to-end with fresh test files
